author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing answers a page number below the first with the first page
summary: A request for the owner listing carrying a page number below the first is answered with the first page of matches, not an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a search matching more than one owner, when a page numbered below the first is asked for, then the first page of matches is listed
given an empty search, when a page numbered below the first is asked for, then the first page of every owner is listed rather than an error page
given any page number below the first — zero and every negative number alike — when the listing is asked for, then the first page is listed
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's handling of the same page numbers — recorded as an open question
the owner listing's answer to a page number past the last page — behavior stays as it is
a page value that is not a number at all
notes: Cause: the owner listing subtracts one from the requested page number before asking for the page, so a value below the first produces an out-of-range request that fails. Fix the boundary in the owner listing only. The two open questions added to docs/prd.md record what this slice deliberately leaves undecided. No Non-Goals row is touched, so no scope_overrides apply.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: No new type, package, or pattern. Page-number normalization belongs at the controller's request-adaptation point, where the existing one-based-to-zero-based translation already lives (OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, line 133-137). Clamping a requested page below the first is binding-time adaptation of an HTTP parameter under the 'Web controller' row of architecture-principles.md (adapts the surface: binds the request, delegates, selects the response), not a business rule -- so the 'no new business rule added to a web controller' bar in that brief's Validation Checklist is not breached, and no service layer is required for this slice. It also places the range control at the trust boundary security-principles.md names ('External input arrives -- validate type, range, and shape before use'), which the current code omits. docs/system-design.md was updated: REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 joins the OwnerController Contracts row, and the 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' paragraph records the normalized-page contract plus the deliberate VetController divergence.
integration_points: The effective page number must reach BOTH the PageRequest and the model. addPaginationModel puts 'currentPage' in the model, and owners/ownersList.html drives the whole pagination widget from it: the current-page highlight (currentPage != i), the first/previous links (currentPage > 1), and the next/last links (currentPage < totalPages). Normalizing inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName alone would return the right rows while rendering a widget that highlights no page and hides the first/previous controls.

processFindForm's other two exits are unaffected: the empty-result branch (rejectValue 'notFound') and the single-match redirect keep their current behavior, since normalization happens before the query.

patterns.description: @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page -- the one-based page contract at the HTTP surface; the default value stays as is
identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) shape in the vet listing -- deliberately NOT changed by this slice (PRD non-goal and open question)

risks.risk: Normalizing at the query helper only, leaving addPaginationModel with the raw requested page, yields correct rows but a broken pagination widget.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once in processFindForm before both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so a single effective page number flows to the query and the model.

risks.risk: Two controllers with an identical page parameter now behave differently, which a reader of this reference sample may read as an inconsistency.
risks.mitigation: The divergence is recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions and now in docs/system-design.md Contracts. Do not extract a shared paging helper for a single caller -- that is a separate slice once the vet question is settled.

risks.risk: Scope creep into adjacent paging edge cases (a page past the last page, a non-numeric page value).
risks.mitigation: Both are explicit PRD non-goals for this slice. A non-numeric value still fails type binding and reaches the error page; leave that path untouched.

risks.risk: Integer overflow at the boundary: Integer.MIN_VALUE would still wrap if the code subtracts one before comparing.
risks.mitigation: Compare and clamp the requested page BEFORE the subtraction, never after.

notes: Autofix audit: the handoff log carries no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit. IDE oracle not connected in this run; the covering-code claims above rest on direct reads of OwnerController.java, VetController.java, and the two Thymeleaf list templates rather than symbol resolution. Test guidance: the two named tests (theOwnerListingShouldReturnTheFirstPageForPageZero, theOwnerListingShouldReturnTheFirstPageForANegativePage) fit the existing MockMvc controller-test pattern in OwnerControllerTests, which is the one sanctioned mock per CLAUDE.md; assert HTTP 200, the owners/ownersList view, and that the model's currentPage is the first page -- the last assertion is what catches a normalization applied only to the query. pageSize stays a local variable; docs/system-design.md Constants already records that it is not a named constant, and promoting it is out of scope here.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Residual, pre-existing, out of scope for this slice: GET /vets.html?page=-2147483648 still reaches PageRequest.of(Integer.MAX_VALUE) via VetController:61, giving an unauthenticated caller a huge-OFFSET query. Low severity on this dataset and already recorded as a PRD open question; worth closing with the same one-line clamp when that question is answered.

Also residual and named as an open question: a page number far past the last one is still passed through on both controllers, so a large positive page produces a large OFFSET scan. Same shape of exposure as the negative case, opposite end of the range.

Supply chain: no dependency, plugin, or version line changed in this diff (build.gradle untouched). The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so no NVD match ran in this review - the resolved set (Spring Boot 4.1.0) is NOT VERIFIED against the NVD here, and that check remains for CI or a human.
approved_aspects: The clamp closes a real unauthenticated-input defect rather than opening one: before the change, GET /owners?page=0 reached PageRequest.of(-1) and raised IllegalArgumentException (a 500 from the error page the PRD already records as leaking technical detail), and page=-2147483648 wrapped page-1 to Integer.MAX_VALUE, producing a ~10.7e9-row OFFSET query. Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is applied before the page-1 translation, so no signed-overflow path survives.

No new trust-boundary surface: the parameter binds as a primitive int, so the clamped value is a number by construction; nothing user-derived reaches shell, SQL string interpolation, file I/O, deserialization, or logging in the diff.

Template safety improved by construction. owners/ownersList.html uses Thymeleaf preprocessing on the model page number (th:href="@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}", lines 44/49/54). Preprocessing evaluated request-derived data is the checklist's own red flag; it stays safe only because the value is an int and can carry no expression text. Feeding the model the effective page rather than the requested one (addPaginationModel(effectivePage, ...)) keeps the pagination links self-consistent and out-of-band values out of that preprocessing.

Class sweep for the same pattern (unclamped external int page reaching PageRequest.of(page - 1)) found exactly two instances repo-wide: OwnerController:141 (fixed) and VetController:61 (unchanged). The divergence is justified in writing at docs/system-design.md and routed to a human as a PRD open question, so it meets the pattern-consistency clause's inline-justification requirement rather than standing as unexplained drift.
No stateful or concurrency change: effectivePage is a method-local, so the singleton controller gains no mutable state.

Tests exercise the boundary value that mattered (Integer.MIN_VALUE, the overflow case) alongside 0 and -1, and assert on the model's currentPage rather than only on the status code, which is what pins the pagination-link behavior.
